results.name: dataset_scope
results.reply: No. The platform does not forecast future prices or demand. It estimates nightly prices for typical listings within each of the ten supported cities based on a snapshot of historical cross-sectional data, not a time series. The estimator uses histogram gradient boosting to predict current market prices given listing attributes like room type, capacity, bedrooms, and amenities. It cannot project how prices or demand will change over time. If you want to explore hosting scenarios—such as comparing estimated nightly prices across neighbourhoods or room types in a city—the Estimator page on index.html is the right tool. For current market context, visit markets.html.

results.name: architecture
results.reply: The platform uses CloudFront and private S3 to serve the frontend (Estimator, Markets, and Project pages). API Gateway routes requests to five focused Lambda functions in private subnets. Authentication: Public estimation and analytics require no sign-in. Saving predictions, viewing private history, and using chat require Cognito authorization with email verification and mandatory TOTP authenticator-app MFA. Data: A cross-sectional snapshot of 279,712 listings across ten cities, processed via Glue and Athena into an S3 data lake. AI services: Bedrock (Claude Haiku) generates assistant text only. A separate scikit-learn histogram gradient boosting model calculates nightly-price estimates. Security includes WAF, KMS encryption, CloudTrail logging, and CloudWatch monitoring.

results.name: diagnostic_not_causal
results.reply: No. The Markets page reports an observed price difference between superhost and non-superhost listings, but that is a descriptive association, not proof of causation. Many unmeasured factors—such as listing quality, location within the neighbourhood, amenities, reviews, or host experience—could explain the difference. The platform lacks the experimental design or causal data needed to conclude that superhost status itself causes higher prices. Use the market analytics to explore hosting scenarios and compare typical listings, but treat observed differences as correlations to investigate further, not as evidence that one feature drives price changes.
